code: # Load bayesplot first so bayesvis functions take precedence in the search path library(bayesplot) #> This is bayesplot version 1.15.0 #> - Online documentation and vignettes at mc-stan.org/bayesplot #> - bayesplot theme set to bayesplot::theme_default() #>    * Does _not_ affect other ggplot2 plots #>    * See ?bayesplot_theme_set for details on theme setting library(bayesvis) #>  #> Attaching package: 'bayesvis' #> The following object is masked from 'package:bayesplot': #>  #>     mcmc_rank_ecdf  # Use a muted color scheme throughout color_scheme_set("blue")

title: Extended Bayesian Visualization: Diagnostics Beyond Trace Plots
text: examples use following synthetic data can reproduce every figure without Stan model.
code: n_iter   <- 1000L   # MCMC iterations per chain n_chains <- 4L      # number of chains n_obs    <- 80L     # observations  # ── Posterior draws ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Six parameters, varying degrees of identifiability. # beta[1]–beta[3]: well identified (posterior SD << prior SD of 1) # beta[4]–beta[6]: weakly identified (posterior SD ≈ prior SD of 1) posterior_2d <- matrix(   c(     rnorm(n_iter, mean =  1.5, sd = 0.12),   # beta[1]     rnorm(n_iter, mean = -0.8, sd = 0.18),   # beta[2]     rnorm(n_iter, mean =  2.1, sd = 0.22),   # beta[3]     rnorm(n_iter, mean =  0.1, sd = 0.94),   # beta[4]     rnorm(n_iter, mean = -0.2, sd = 0.98),   # beta[5]     rnorm(n_iter, mean =  0.3, sd = 0.91)    # beta[6]   ),   ncol = 6L ) colnames(posterior_2d) <- paste0("beta[", 1:6, "]") prior_sd <- rep(1, 6)  # ── Well-mixing 3D array ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Four chains, two parameters: draws are i.i.d. so mixing is perfect. good_array <- array(   rnorm(n_iter * n_chains * 2),   dim      = c(n_iter, n_chains, 2L),   dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("chain:", 1:4), c("mu", "sigma")) )  # ── Badly-mixing 3D array ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Chain 1 for "mu" is stuck in a completely different region. bad_array         <- good_array bad_array[, 1, 1] <- rnorm(n_iter, mean = 8, sd = 0.15)  # ── Observed data and posterior predictive draws ───────────────────────────── y_true <- 2 y      <- rnorm(n_obs, mean = y_true, sd = 1)  # Well-calibrated model: yrep drawn from the same distribution as y yrep_good   <- matrix(rnorm(500L * n_obs, mean = y_true, sd = 1), nrow = 500L)  # Over-confident model: posterior predictive intervals too narrow yrep_narrow <- matrix(rnorm(500L * n_obs, mean = y_true, sd = 0.25), nrow = 500L)  # ── LOO-PIT values ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Well-calibrated ≈ Uniform(0,1) pit_good  <- runif(n_obs) # Over-dispersed: PIT concentrated near 0 and 1 pit_over  <- rbeta(n_obs, shape1 = 0.35, shape2 = 0.35) # Under-dispersed: PIT concentrated near 0.5 pit_under <- rbeta(n_obs, shape1 = 5, shape2 = 5)

text: shrinkage factor κθ=1−Var̂(θ∣y)Var̂(θ)\kappa_\theta = 1 - \frac{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\theta \mid y)}   {\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\theta)} measures much posterior contracted relative prior. κ≈1\kappa \approx 1: data highly informative θ\theta (posterior much tighter prior). κ≈0\kappa \approx 0: posterior barely updated prior (weakly identified parameter). Plotting κ\kappa posterior z-score zθ=θ‾post/SD̂(θ∣y)z_\theta = \bar\theta_{\text{post}} / \widehat{\text{SD}}(\theta \mid y) reveals signal--noise ratio parameter simultaneously.

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf
text: Plots empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) within-chain rank statistics alongside simultaneous confidence band consistent ideal mixing. good mixing ECDFs chains indistinguishable lie within band around diagonal. Chains explore different regions posterior show ECDFs diverge diagonal . ECDF-based companion bayesplot::mcmc_rank_overlay() implements diagnostic described Vehtari et al. (2021).

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf
text: x 3D numeric array MCMC draws dimensions [iterations × chains × parameters]. dimnames attribute used chain parameter labels; missing names auto-generated. pars Optional character vector parameter names plot. Names must match third dimension x. NULL (default), parameters shown. prob Numeric (0, 1). Coverage probability simultaneous confidence band (DKW inequality). Default 0.99. facet_args named list additional arguments forwarded ggplot2::facet_wrap(), ncol scales. Ignored one parameter plotted.

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf
text: ggplot2::ggplot object. multiple parameters shown, plot faceted parameter.

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf
text: parameter, draws chains pooled ranked (average ties). ECDF resulting within-chain ranks plotted chain probability scale \([0, 1]\) (ranks divided total number draws \(S = \times C\)). ideal mixing ranks exchangeable across chains, chain's ECDF track diagonal. simultaneous band uses Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz (DKW) inequality: $$\Pr\!\left(\sup_x |F_I(x) - F(x)| \leq \varepsilon\right) \geq   1 - 2e^{-2 \varepsilon^2}$$ \(\) number iterations per chain, giving: $$\varepsilon = \sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\alpha)}{2I}}$$

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf

title: Rank-based ECDF plots per chain — mcmc_rank_ecdf
code: set.seed(7)  # Well-mixing chains: ECDFs should stay within the confidence band good <- array(   rnorm(500 * 4 * 2),   dim      = c(500, 4, 2),   dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("chain:", 1:4), c("mu", "sigma")) ) mcmc_rank_ecdf(good)   # Pathological mixing: first chain stuck in a different region bad <- good bad[, 1, 1] <- rnorm(500, mean = 10, sd = 0.2) mcmc_rank_ecdf(bad, pars = "mu")   # Adjust number of facet columns mcmc_rank_ecdf(good, facet_args = list(ncol = 1))

Shrinkage quantifies much posterior contracted relative prior: \(\kappa \approx 1\) means data highly informative parameter; \(\kappa \approx 0\) means posterior barely updated prior. diagnostic especially useful regularized regression hierarchical models parameters may weakly identified, part simulation-based calibration (SBC) workflows.

title: Prior-to-posterior shrinkage diagnostic plot — mcmc_shrinkage
text: shrinkage factor parameter \(\theta\) defined : $$\kappa_\theta = 1 - \frac{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\theta \mid y)}   {\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\theta)}$$ numerator sample variance posterior draws denominator prior variance (supplied via prior_sd estimated prior_draws). Values clamped [0, 1]. z-score ratio posterior mean posterior SD: $$z_\theta = \frac{\bar{\theta}_{\text{post}}}   {\widehat{\operatorname{SD}}(\theta \mid y)}$$ serving signal--noise measure. Parameters \(|z| > 2\) high \(\kappa\) well-identified. Parameters low \(\kappa\) regardless z-score suggest weak identifiability near-prior posteriors. Reference lines drawn \(\kappa \\{0, 0.5, 1\}\) \(z = 0\).

title: Prior-to-posterior shrinkage diagnostic plot — mcmc_shrinkage
code: set.seed(42) n_iter <- 1000  # Six parameters: first three have high shrinkage (informative data), # last three have low shrinkage (weakly identified / near-prior) posterior <- matrix(   c(rnorm(n_iter * 3, mean = 1.5, sd = 0.15),  # high shrinkage     rnorm(n_iter * 3, mean = 0.0, sd = 0.95)),  # low shrinkage   ncol = 6 ) colnames(posterior) <- paste0("beta[", 1:6, "]")  mcmc_shrinkage(posterior, prior_sd = 1)   # Using prior draws instead of closed-form prior SDs prior_draws <- matrix(rnorm(n_iter * 6, sd = 1), ncol = 6) colnames(prior_draws) <- colnames(posterior) mcmc_shrinkage(posterior, prior_draws = prior_draws)   # Select a subset of parameters mcmc_shrinkage(posterior, prior_sd = 1, pars = paste0("beta[", 4:6, "]"))

title: Posterior predictive coverage plot — ppc_coverage
text: observed data point, computes credible interval posterior predictive draws marks whether observation covered. Observations displayed sorted x-axis, intervals colored coverage status empirical coverage rate annotated. Departures nominal prob coverage indicate model mis-specification: Empirical coverage < nominal: model -confident (intervals narrow). Empirical coverage > nominal: model -confident (intervals wide).

title: Posterior predictive coverage plot — ppc_coverage
code: ppc_coverage(   y,   yrep,   prob = 0.9,   sort_by = c("y", "mean", "index"),   point_size = 1.5,   interval_linewidth = 0.4 )

title: Posterior predictive coverage plot — ppc_coverage
text: y numeric vector observed data values (length \(n\)). yrep numeric matrix posterior predictive draws (\(S \times n\)), \(S\) number draws \(n = \text{length}(y)\). prob Numeric (0, 1). Nominal coverage probability predictive intervals. Default 0.90. sort_by Character string. order observations x-axis: "y" Sort observed value (default). Makes coverage gaps near tails easy spot. "mean" Sort posterior predictive mean. "index" Preserve original observation order. point_size Numeric. Size observed-value points. Default 1.5. interval_linewidth Numeric. Width interval line segments. Default 0.4.

title: Posterior predictive coverage plot — ppc_coverage
code: set.seed(99) n    <- 60 y    <- rnorm(n, mean = 2, sd = 1) yrep <- matrix(rnorm(500 * n, mean = 2, sd = 1), nrow = 500)  # Well-calibrated model: empirical coverage ≈ nominal 90% ppc_coverage(y, yrep, prob = 0.90)   # Over-confident model: intervals are too narrow yrep_narrow <- matrix(rnorm(500 * n, mean = 2, sd = 0.25), nrow = 500) ppc_coverage(y, yrep_narrow, prob = 0.90)   # Sort by posterior predictive mean instead of observed value ppc_coverage(y, yrep, sort_by = "mean")
